body.statement: Conditional on \(z_0\) and the exact path-design array, the donor experiment is independent of the joint training-response and treated-event experiment, and its conditional kernel is the product of the \(N\) one-donor kernels. The remaining conditional kernel factors across joint within-unit histories, but need not factor between pre-event responses and treated event outcomes. Because every \(X_{st}\) is observed exactly, no convolution operator acts on a training coordinate.
body.justification: The factorization rigorously separates donor uncertainty from the joint panel while preserving unrestricted within-unit training/event dependence beyond the two conditional means.
body.gap: Generated-regressor and errors-in-variables experiments do not share this exact-training-coordinate kernel.
body.consumer: Data provenance determines whether the first stage calls for a location modulus or deconvolution.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{st})_{s,t})\), let
\(\mathcal Z=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\), and let \(\mathcal U\) be the
sigma-field generated jointly by all untreated responses and all treated event
outcomes.  Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} says, conditional
on \(z_0\), that \(\mathcal Z\) is independent of
\(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal U\).  Thus, for \(A\in\mathcal Z\) and
\(D\in\mathcal U\), the tower property and conditional independence give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(A\cap D\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 &=E[\mathbf 1_D E(\mathbf 1_A\mid z_0,\mathcal X,\mathcal U)
       \mid z_0,\mathcal X]\\
 &=E[\mathbf 1_D P(A\mid z_0)\mid z_0,\mathcal X]\\
 &=P(A\mid z_0)P(D\mid z_0,\mathcal X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-independence} makes the first factor the product
of the \(N\) one-donor conditional kernels.  Assumption
\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes the second factor a product over
the joint within-unit histories indexed by \((s,i)\).  It does not split the
pre-event and event coordinates within one such history.

The latter qualification is substantive and remains true after adding
\texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  For example, condition on an exact
design, take independent centered Rademacher variables \(U_{si}\) across
\((s,i)\), and, for a sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), set
\[
 Q_{s1i}=m_s(X_{s1})+\varepsilon U_{si},
 \qquad
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b_s+\varepsilon U_{si}.
\]
Use fresh independent centered bounded errors in the other windows.  Then
\(E[Q_{s1i}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{s1})\) and
\(E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=b_s
=E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]\), while the two displayed variables are
dependent conditional on \((z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The support restriction is
preserved by taking \(\varepsilon\) small, and the corresponding potential
outcomes can be centered to satisfy event-date transport and consistency.
Hence no stronger within-unit product factorization follows.

Finally, \texttt{ass:center-only-design} places the exact \(X_{st}\), not a
noisy surrogate, in \(\mathcal X\).  Therefore the response kernel is
conditioned directly on its regression coordinate; there is no measurement-
error convolution and hence no deconvolution operator on a training
coordinate.
